Main.sentence: Bernard Jeffrey McCullough (October 5, 1957 – August 9, 2008)  , known professionally as Bernie Mac , was an American stand-up comedian, actor and film producer.

His most noted film roles were as Frank Catton in the ___E:Ocean's film series U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean%27s_(franchise))___ from 2001 through 2007 and as the title character of Mr. 3000 .

Mac joined ___E:Steve Harvey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Harvey)___ , ___E:Cedric the Entertainer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer)___ , and ___E:D. L. Hughley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._L._Hughley)___ as one of the "Big Four" comedians in the film The Original Kings of Comedy .
After briefly hosting the ___E:HBO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO)___ show Midnight Mac , Mac appeared in several films in smaller roles.

He was the star of The Bernie Mac Show , which ran from 2001 through 2006, earning him two ___E:Emmy Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award)___ nominations for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series.
His other films included starring roles in The Players Club , Head of State , Bad Santa , Guess Who , Pride , and Soul Men .
Mac died at 50 years old on August 9, 2008 in Chicago, Illinois of complications from pneumonia.
Bernard Jeffrey McCullough was born on October 5, 1957 in ___E:Chicago, Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago,_Illinois)___ .
Mac was the second child of Mary McCullough and Jeffrey Harrison.
Mac was raised by his single mother and his grandparents on the city's south side.
Mac began his high school career at ___E:Chicago Vocational High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Vocational_High_School)___ .

During 1973, Mac moved to ___E:Tampa, Florida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tampa,_Florida)___ , to attend ___E:Jesuit High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesuit_High_School_(Tampa))___ following the death of his mother during his sophomore year.  Shortly afterward, Mac's older brother and his estranged father both died. Mac later returned to Chicago and graduated from Chicago Vocational in 1975.

During his 20s and through his early 30s, Mac worked in a variety of jobs, including janitor, coach, professional mover, cook, bus driver, Wonder Bread delivery man, furniture mover, and ___E:UPS U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Parcel_Service)___ agent, while doing comedy on the weekends at clubs and parties.

Mac's influences were from ___E:The Three Stooges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Three_Stooges)___ and listening to stand-up comedians ___E:Richard Pryor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Pryor)___ and ___E:Redd Foxx U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Redd_Foxx)___ .

Mac started as a stand-up comedian in Chicago's Cotton Club. After he won the ___E:Miller Lite Comedy Search U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miller_Lite_Comedy_Search)___ at the age of 32, his popularity as a comedian began to grow. In 1992, a performance on the 3rd episode of ___E:HBO U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO)___ 's Def Comedy Jam thrust him into the spotlight; after ___E:Martin Lawrence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Lawrence)___ was unable to calm an increasingly hostile crowd, Mac went onstage and told the audience "I ain't scared o' you mothafuckas" and that he "didn't come here for no foolishness."
In 2001, the Fox network gave Mac his own television sitcom called The Bernie Mac Show portraying a ___E:fictional version of himself U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_McCullough)___ .

In the show, he suddenly becomes ___E:custodian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_guardian)___ of his sister's three children after she enters ___E:rehab U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_rehabilitation)___ .
Mac broke the ___E:fourth wall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_wall)___ to tell his thoughts to the audience.

The show contained many parodies of events in Bernie's actual life. Mac, who grew up on Chicago's South Side, was a fan of the ___E:Chicago White Sox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox)___ , and would often sneak a reference to his favorite team in episodes, including enlisting then-White Sox pitcher ___E:Jon Garland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Garland)___ to make a guest cameo appearance.

In the 2005 season he wore a White Sox jacket and cap, and congratulated his hometown ___E:Chicago White Sox U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox)___ and their staff members on their recent World Series championship.
The show was not renewed after the 2005–2006 season.

The series finale aired on April 14, 2006. Among other awards, the show won an ___E:Emmy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award)___  for "Outstanding Writing", the ___E:Peabody Award U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Award)___ for excellence in broadcasting, and the ___E:Humanitas Prize U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humanitas_Prize)___ for television writing that promotes human dignity.
His character on The Bernie Mac Show was ranked No. 47 in TV Guide 's list of the "50 Greatest TV Dads of All Time".

During his run on the show, Mac had co-starring roles in the ___E:Ocean's trilogy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocean%27s_(film_series))___ (2001–2007), Head of State (2003) and Bad Santa (2003), as well as starring roles in the baseball-themed film Mr. 3000 (2004) and Guess Who? (2005), a remake of the 1967 film Guess Who's Coming to Dinner .

On March 19, 2007, Mac told ___E:David Letterman U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Letterman)___ on the CBS Late Show that he would retire from his 30-year career after he finished shooting the comedy film, The Whole Truth, Nothing but the Truth, So Help Me Mac . "I'm going to still do my producing, my films, but I want to enjoy my life a little bit", Mac told Letterman. "I missed a lot of things, you know. I was a street performer for two years.
I went into clubs in 1977 and was on the road 47 weeks out of the year."

During this time, Mac was having success as a popular film actor, starting with an appearance in the 2007 film Transformers as the car salesman "Bobby Bolivia", and serving as the voice of Zuba, Alex the Lion's long-lost father in Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa .
He co-starred with ___E:Samuel L. Jackson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_L._Jackson)___ in the 2008 musical comedy Soul Men .
The latter two films were released months after his death.
His final film role was as Jimmy Lunchbox in the 2009 film Old Dogs which was released a year after his death.
Mac married his high school sweetheart Rhonda Gore on September 17, 1977, and together they had a daughter in 1978.

In the last 20 years of his life, Mac publicly disclosed that he had severe ___E:sarcoidosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcoidosis)___ , a disease of unknown origin that causes inflammation in tissue.

On July 19, 2008, Mac was admitted to the ___E:Northwestern Memorial Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northwestern_Memorial_Hospital)___ in his hometown of ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ .

After being treated in the ICU for three weeks for pneumonia, Mac went into cardiac arrest and subsequently died during the early morning hours on August 9, at the age of 50. However, the complications were not attributed to his sarcoidosis, according to his publicist.
Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa and Soul Men were released posthumously and dedicated to his memory.
Mac's public memorial was held a week after his death at the House of Hope Church, with nearly 7,000 people in attendance.

Notable mourners at Mac's funeral were ___E:Chris Rock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock)___ , ___E:Chicago Mayor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Chicago)___ ___E:Richard M. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_M._Daley)___ , ___E:Samuel L. Jackson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_L._Jackson)___ , ___E:Ashton Kutcher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashton_Kutcher)___ , ___E:Don Cheadle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle)___ , the cast members from The Bernie Mac Show , and his Kings of Comedy fellows ___E:D. L. Hughley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._L._Hughley)___ , ___E:Cedric the Entertainer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer)___ , and ___E:Steve Harvey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Harvey)___ .

The first two of Mac's posthumous films, Soul Men and Madagascar: Escape 2 Africa , were released three months after his death and were dedicated to him. Mac's third posthumously released and final film, Old Dogs , was released a year after his death; it too was dedicated in part to Mac. The 2008 ___E:Bud Billiken Parade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Billiken_Parade_and_Picnic)___ , which was held in Chicago on the day of Mac's death, was also dedicated to his memory.

On the day of Mac's funeral, his hometown's local television station ___E:WCIU-TV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WCIU-TV)___ aired an exclusive television special, A Tribute to Bernie Mac , and had interviews with his former colleagues including ___E:Camille Winbush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_Winbush)___ , ___E:Chris Rock U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock)___ , ___E:Joe Torry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Torry)___ , ___E:Cameron Diaz U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Diaz)___ , ___E:Don Cheadle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Cheadle)___ , and some of his family members & close friends.

During ___E:Steve Harvey's television show U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Harvey_(talk_show))___ which aired November 14, 2016, Harvey read a proclamation from Chicago's Mayor ___E:Rahm Emanuel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rahm_Emanuel)___ proclaiming November 14 as "Bernie Mac Day".

Steve Harvey's guests included Bernie's wife Rhonda, their daughter Je'Niece, granddaughter Jasmine, and Bernie's The Original Kings of Comedy co-stars ___E:D. L. Hughley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D._L._Hughley)___ , ___E:Cedric the Entertainer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer)___ , and ___E:Guy Torry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guy_Torry)___ (who was the original host at the beginning of the tour). ___E:Mike Epps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Epps)___ , appearing via satellite, along with the principal of Bernie and Rhonda's alma mater ___E:Chicago Vocational High School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Vocational_High_School)___ (CVS), revealed and unveiled the renaming of CVS Auditorium to the "Bernie Mac Auditorium".
On February 14, 2017, Rolling Stone named Bernie Mac #41 of the 50 Best Stand-Up Comics of All Time.
